author: Linnaeus, 1758
summary: 해마다 수백 마리가 우리나라를 지나가는 나그네새로, 호수와 늪, 소택지에서 지낸다. 벼와 풀씨, 물속 곤충, 갑각류 등을 먹는다. 온대에서 아한대에 걸친 지역에서 번식하며, 물가 풀숲이나 숲속 땅 위에 풀로 둥지를 짓고 알 8~14개를 낳는다. 아시아, 유럽, 북아메리카에 분포한다.

sexes.male: 머리와 뒷목, 등, 가슴이 검은 갈색이고 눈 위에서 윗목까지 흰 눈썹선이 뚜렷하며, 아랫면은 잿빛을 띤 흰색이다.
sexes.female: 몸이 얼룩진 갈색이고 부리 기부에 연한 얼룩무늬가 있다.

art.subject: Garganey (Spatula querquedula), adult male in breeding plumage, as seen in Korea on spring passage in March and April: head and neck rich chocolate-brown, finely streaked white on the cheeks and neck; a bold, broad white supercilium curving from above the eye down to the upper hindneck; crown dark blackish-brown; breast warm brown with dense dark scalloping; flanks pale grey finely vermiculated, cleanly cut off from the brown breast; long drooping black-and-white striped scapulars hanging over the flanks; belly greyish-white; rear end mottled brown. Bill dark grey to blackish; iris dark brown; legs grey.
art.pose: dabbling at the edge of a marshy pond, side view
art.scene: Korean spring migration in March and April: a reed-fringed freshwater pond and marsh with the first green growth; no people, buildings or text
views: adult male breeding, side view swimming: chocolate-brown head with a broad white supercilium curving to the upper neck, scaly brown breast, pale grey flanks, drooping black-and-white scapulars, dark grey bill
adult female, side view swimming: mottled brown body, dark eye-stripe and pale supercilium, whitish loral spot at the base of the bill, dark line across the cheek, whitish throat, plain grey bill
adult male, flight from above: pale blue-grey forewing, green speculum with white borders, brown head and breast
art.build: Small dabbling duck, about 38cm, clearly smaller than a Mallard and close to a Eurasian Teal in size. Head rather long with a flat crown; bill straight, dark, about as long as the head, of ordinary duck shape. Legs short, grey. Swims and dabbles at the edges of pools and marshes, often in pairs or small groups on migration. At rest the wingtips reach the base of the tail. Tail short and pointed. In flight the male shows a pale blue-grey forewing and a green speculum bordered white in front and behind.
avoid: Do not give the male a chestnut head with a green eye patch or a white vertical stripe at the breast side; that is Eurasian Teal.
Do not paint a broad spoon-shaped bill (Northern Shoveler) or a yellow or orange bill.
Do not shorten the white supercilium to a small eyebrow; it is broad and runs down to the hindneck.
